findings.summary: The code-health writers can still skip the builder: they pass a plain &str to Athena::queue.
findings.evidence: Athena::queue (reading.rs:550) takes &str. A StewardRequest whose render() returns a String still lets a new hook writer call self.queue with any text. Only the all-writers test, which lists the writers known today, would catch it. Criterion 4 asks for enforcement by mechanism, not convention. Fix: Add a queue method that takes a StewardRequest (for example Athena::queue_steward(&StewardRequest)) and use it for the structural pass and the design review. Then the type, not only the test, enforces the format for in-process writers.

findings.summary: Criterion 3's reopen test already passes on the base commit, so it guards against regressions but does not show a change.
findings.evidence: structural_pass_open already returns false for JobState::Closed(_) (code_health.rs:520). The plan states this, but its 'fails without the behavior' line describes a hypothetical regression. Fix: Keep the test. In the change description and CHANGELOG entry, say plainly that the dedupe already ignored closed passes, and that this job adds a test and a doc fix for it rather than a code change.

findings.summary: Default bullets for model-written follow-ups could be too generic to be checked.
findings.evidence: RequestQueue::apply (steward.rs:449-465) uses change.request as the text. With no bullets in the text, the defaults alone pass the parser but may not say what done means for that follow-up. Fix: Keep any bullets already in change.request. Default bullets should name the source (change.source) and the work item's title, plus the fmt, clippy and test bullet, so the planner gets checkable acceptance.

findings.summary: The structural-pass and design-review requests stay on the cli channel, not the steward channel.
findings.evidence: Athena::queue writes channel "cli", while REQUEST_CHANNEL is "steward" (steward.rs:326). The request calls these writers steward-channel writers. Fix: Leaving the channel as is is acceptable. Mention it in the CHANGELOG or the change description so readers are not surprised.

summary: I read code_health.rs, reading.rs and steward.rs, and the plan holds up against them. `plan_entry` (reading.rs:1648-1664) counts every bullet line anywhere in an unread request as acceptance, and every path-like word as a touched file. `structural_text` (code_health.rs:481) emits no bullets, so the plan correctly puts the fault in the writers. The design-review text writes `   - <job> (...)` lines (code_health.rs:611) that the parser would read as acceptance, and the plan already rewords those. `structural_pass_open` (code_health.rs:515-521) already skips `JobState::Closed`, so for the dedupe part a test plus a doc fix is honest and enough. Moving the parse into pub functions that `plan_entry` calls lets the tests run the real parse. Routing `RequestQueue::apply` through `from_change` covers the model-written follow-ups and blind spots on the steward channel. I found no blocker or major problem. Three minor points remain: the hook writers can still bypass the builder, criterion 3's test passes even without this change, and default bullets for model-written follow-ups could be too generic.
